title: urnetwork / taskworker
description: Authenticated Taskworker deep dive. Task names come only from the finite registered target set; attribution is system or client without identity labels. Queue and aggregate exporter values are shown only with their owning fresh snapshot. Missing or stale telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: task submissions, finishes and failures / s
panels.description: Committed new task submissions and finished tasks across all scraped producer services in the selected env. Includes continuations and RunOnce successors. Rollbacks are excluded from submitted/finished; completion may leave a durable post retry. Function failures count returned errors before retry writes or finalization. Finalization failures separately count each participating task in a failed handback invocation, including unknown commit replies; a function may have succeeded. These populations overlap and must not be summed. Repeated attempts count again; these are not distinct tasks or financial commits. Graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded from function failures; other cancellations remain failures. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: function failures by target / s
panels.description: Failed function attempts per finite registered target (task label = package.function) across all scraped producer services in the selected env, summed over caller attribution and typed causes. Uses the same function-failure scope as the adjacent total: graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded; other cancellations remain failures. Repeated failures count again; missing targets appear as unregistered. This counts function outcomes before retry writes or finalization, not committed task or financial work. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: finalization failures by target, phase and cause / s
panels.description: Failed finalization invocations per participating task by finite registered target, source phase and typed cause. Count each distinct member once in a failed batch or cohort; safe single fallback is a new attempt and delegation is counted once. Pre-transaction compatibility fallback is excluded. The phase marks the operation entered before terminal failure, not necessarily the first causal fault; a returned Post error followed by an aborted-transaction write appears at queue_update. Acquire does not identify Ping versus pool capacity; admission is pre-BEGIN business ownership. Includes unknown commit replies: the commit may have succeeded. Acknowledged identifies a failure observed after confirmed commit, not rollback. External task-post results are outside this counter. Older binaries may have the aggregate failure counter without phase telemetry. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: ready workers
panels.description: Instances whose startup readiness latch is set; this does not prove current task execution or finalization progress.

panels.title: executions in flight
panels.description: Registered task functions currently running, across system and client-attributed work.

panels.title: fresh available queue depth
panels.description: Maximum replica observation of available rows from one database snapshot, shown only while the snapshot is under 45 seconds old. Exact up to 10,000 available rows; past that a planner estimate, flagged in fresh queue depth by state.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!="",state="available"} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: fresh oldest overdue task
panels.description: Seconds past run_at for the oldest available row, only from a fresh bounded queue snapshot. The snapshot reads the first 10,000 available rows in poll order, which is every available row unless the available depth is estimated.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_oldest_overdue_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: task executions by outcome
panels.description: Execution starts and bounded terminal outcomes per finite registered task.

panels.title: system vs client-attributed executions
panels.description: Task metadata distinguishes system work from client-attributed work without retaining a client identity label.

panels.title: mean execution duration
panels.description: Rate-derived mean function duration per registered task and attribution.

targets.expr: sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_sum{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_count{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: fresh one-minute maximum execution duration
panels.description: Exact process maxima only while the owning completion is under 120 seconds old; idle tasks remain no-data.

targets.expr: max by (task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: tasks balked / s (RunOnce conflicts)
panels.description: RunOnce conflicts across all scraped producer services in the selected env, including accepted coalescing and IfAbsent refusals. An active conflict may still request a later run. Rolled-back attempts are excluded; host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: task argument and result bytes / s
panels.description: Serialized input and already-produced output bytes; payload contents and identities are never labels.

panels.title: fresh queue depth by state
panels.description: Database-wide total, available, claimed, and reschedule_error states. Max across replicas avoids multiplying the shared queue; samples expire after 45 seconds. Each side of the availability boundary is counted exactly up to 10,000 rows; past that a state is a planner estimate, and claimed a lower bound, shown as 1 by its estimated series on the right axis.

targets.expr: max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth_estimated{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: poll and queue snapshot pressure
panels.description: EvalTasks claim/empty/error outcomes plus bounded queue snapshot failures.

panels.title: finalization and reschedule outcomes
panels.description: Acknowledged completion, reschedule and post-hook reschedule outcomes after task execution. Failed or unacknowledged finalization attempts are shown separately at the top. External post errors are not counted here.

panels.title: lease refresh failures
panels.description: Task timestamp lease refresh errors; these can strand claimed work and deserve separate visibility from function outcomes.

panels.title: drain and final handback
panels.description: Tasks in flight at drain start, tasks canceled and rescheduled, and drain duration. The runner flushes metrics after final handback.

panels.title: subscription aggregate exporter freshness
panels.description: Age of the freshest complete subscription snapshot. Values beyond 20 minutes are intentionally omitted by the subscriptions dashboard and §2.27 signal.

panels.title: egress probe fleet exporter
panels.description: Fresh completed provider-fleet snapshot controls; the dedicated egress board owns full outcome interpretation.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: Postgres and Redis pressure
panels.description: Initialized Postgres pool occupancy plus Redis connection and timeout controls.

panels.title: Postgres acquire and lifecycle pressure
panels.description: Acquire outcomes/wait and connection creation/destruction expose taskworker database saturation.

panels.title: process CPU, memory, and goroutines
panels.description: Taskworker process saturation controls by selected deploy block and host.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores active phase spans
panels.description: Current spans by worker and phase. target_export is the parent of target_map, gob_encode, and cache_write. Parallel work can activate several spans; do not sum parent and child phases.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores completed phase wall time / s
panels.description: Wall seconds accumulated by completed spans per second. Concurrent spans can exceed one second per second, and target_export includes child phases. This measures wall time, not CPU time; active spans contribute only when they exit.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase exits / s
panels.description: Phase exits per second including error and panic cleanup. An exit does not imply success; rates describe distinct phase lifecycles.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase work items / s
panels.description: Work units per second: source_load rows, target_export passes, target_map/filter inputs inspected, gob_encode values, and cache_write Redis SET attempts. Units differ by phase, and retries contribute additional attempts.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase workload bytes / s
panels.description: Bytes produced by gob_encode or submitted as Redis key and value bytes in cache_write SET attempts, including retries. Other phases are zero. These are workload bytes, not heap allocations or confirmed Redis writes.

panels.title: failed finalization mean elapsed by phase
panels.description: Mean whole failed-invocation wall time including rollback and cleanup, grouped by entered source phase. One latency observation per finalizer invocation; a shared batch/cohort is one observation while its error counter counts participating tasks. This is not phase-only time, SQL runtime, or financial rollback latency. No successful attempts are included. External task-post joins after finalizer return are outside this measurement. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: payer debit batches / s by result
panels.description: Asynchronous payer debit batches by result; not contract throughput or provider payout.

panels.title: debit worker owners by shard
panels.description: Current bounded debit worker owners by partition and reporting process.

panels.title: oldest retained debit by shard
panels.description: Oldest retained debit age by worker partition, including committed records awaiting their Redis release.

panels.title: debit worker observation and completion age
panels.description: Time since the last successful oldest-debit observation (including empty partitions) and since the last debit-worker completion without a failed balance. Busy balances can remain pending after a completion.

panels.title: finalization admission errors and skipped lease refreshes / s
panels.description: Failed finalization admission attempts per participating task by entered stage and cause (an acknowledged busy wait does not prove one continuous wait), and task timestamp hints skipped because ownership was busy or the claim no longer matched.

panels.title: account outbox deliveries and payout wallet sources / s
panels.description: Account message outbox deliveries by template and result, and release payout providers by the source that selected their wallet, or why none was selected.

panels.title: claims handed back to a newer config / s
panels.description: URL probe passes, disabled markers, contract degradation checks and verification chains that a taskworker claimed and handed back unchanged, because a newer config's live stamp owns them, by task family. A steady rate means taskworkers on an older config run beside a newer one: narrow the host to find them. Their claims cycle back to the newer config's instances until they restart on it.

panels.title: idle run-once chain wakes / s
panels.description: A recurring run-once chain that finds no work backs off to its idle delay and sets a wake mark in Redis (marked); once it runs at its active cadence again it removes its own mark (resumed). A producer in any service clears the marks of the chains its committed work feeds: active, the chain had no mark (one Redis round trip, no queue write); kicked, this producer removed the mark and pulled the chain's pending row to now; busy, the chain's queue key was held, so its holder reads the new work; due, the row was already due. error: a mark, clear or kick that failed; the chain still runs at its idle delay. Producers run in every service, so the host and block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: client location reliability pass: clients and rows written
panels.description: What the last client location reliability pass (UpdateClientLocationReliabilities) each taskworker ran computed: its clients by identity kind (hosted_child, a hosted child identity with source_client_id set, which most readers exclude; top_level, the rest), and the rows its upsert inserted or rewrote. A connected client's row is rewritten only when a value changed or once a day, so rows written far under the clients means the pass left unchanged rows alone. Each process keeps the numbers of the last pass it ran until it runs another; rows written is shown only for processes that have run a pass.

targets.expr: max by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_written_rows{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) and on (host, block, instance) count by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_clients{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: points leaderboard: payments earning in payout weeks
panels.description: How approximate the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published is (RebuildPointsLeaderboard, owner decision 2026-10-28). Blocks and Streak publish as soon as a completed operator block exists; a payment whose paid sweeps the history rollup has not measured earns in its payout weeks, every block from its oldest paid sweep to the end of its plan's traffic window, an upper bound of its measured blocks. rollup_pending payments are those, and stored rows replace their weeks as the rollup measures them; sweeps_reaped are completed payments the rollup measured after contract reaping had deleted their sweeps, whose weeks stay. rollup pending payments is the rollup's remaining work in any block; it should fall while the rebuild runs every minute. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: points leaderboard: approximate networks and unlinked points
panels.description: What the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published counted: networks with a positive point among its payout-week or unlinked inputs, whose Blocks and Streak are approximate (never below their measured values), and positive post-genesis point rows without a payment row, each earning in the last block that closed before it posted. Unlinked points have no sweeps to measure; points-readiness warns while any exist. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest SN Top snapshot (LEADERTOP.md) each taskworker computed or read was computed. A snapshot folds one tempo of about 72 minutes, a few minutes after it ends; the apps call the board stale past three tempos (about 3.6 hours). No data before the process saw a snapshot, or while st is disabled.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot counts
panels.description: What the newest SN Top snapshot each taskworker wrote counted, by kind: ranked networks, verify-eligible providers, measured providers (the verify cohort), claimed fleets (UIDs), open head seats and the non-seed hops of complete trails in the tempo. Counts only, no identities.

panels.title: SN Top board: Top 200 line and claimed floor
panels.description: The newest snapshot's projected 200th score (the Top 200 line every margin and label is measured from; 0 while fewer than 200 networks rank) and the floor among the claimed fleets the replica selects (no data without a claimed fleet).

panels.title: SN Top board: agreement with the validator and the chain
panels.description: Per folded tempo: UIDs whose replica score equals (match) or differs from (mismatch) the validator's exact head summary score, where any mismatch means the replica is wrong; and UIDs the validator selected that earn (earning) or do not earn (not_earning) on-chain incentive. All are 0 until fleets bind and the head summary and incentive reads arrive (LEADERTOP.md §6.3).

panels.title: SN Top board: precision at 200
panels.description: Of the claimed networks the previous snapshot projected inside the Top 200, the share the validator then selected. No data until fleets bind and a head summary arrives. The board's likely label turns on only at 0.9 or above (owner decision Q17); below that every row inside the line shows estimate.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot runs
panels.description: How long each taskworker's newest SN Top snapshot took to read its inputs, project and write, in seconds, and how many snapshots it wrote in the last hour (about one a tempo, 0.83 an hour). A process that checks but finds no completed tempo writes none.

panels.title: reaper mode
panels.description: The mode the newest reaper run read from its Redis control {contract_horizon}control: off reads and deletes nothing; dry run reads and classifies each batch but deletes nothing and never advances the cursor; on deletes. The code default is off, so a deploy deletes nothing until an operator sets the mode. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_mode{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: horizon (days)
panels.description: How long past its creation and its close a contract is kept, as the newest run's control read set it: horizonDays, whole days from 35 to 91, or the code's 91 days while the control sets none. A contract minted and closed before now less the horizon is past it. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) / 86400

panels.title: pass lag behind the horizon
panels.description: How far the pass's cursor is behind the horizon: the horizon time less the mint time of the last contract the pass committed past. It falls while the pass catches up and is near zero once the pass reaches the horizon. A pass that reached the horizon starts over from the oldest contract once it began 30 days ago (the rescan), so the lag jumps then. Off and dry run never advance the cursor, so their lag grows. No data before the pass committed a batch. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_lag_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: pass cursor (contract mint time)
panels.description: Mint time of the last contract id the pass committed past, where the next run resumes. Only an on batch advances it. No data before the pass committed a batch. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: pass started
panels.description: When the current pass started at the oldest contract. A pass that reaches the horizon starts over once it began 30 days ago, to revisit the contracts it kept. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_pass_start_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: newest run started
panels.description: When the newest reaper run any taskworker still reports started: the horizon time it published plus the horizon. A run lasts about 10 minutes at most; the next follows 15 seconds later while the pass has work left, and 5 minutes later once it reached the horizon, found the reaper off or ran a dry run. A start older than about 15 minutes means the chain is not running, and the other reaper stats show No data past 30 minutes. A run that cannot read its control publishes nothing.

panels.title: reaper rows deleted / s by table
panels.description: Rows the reaper deleted, by table. Each contract goes in one transaction with its close reports, closes, escrows, sweeps and extender parties, so transfer_contract is the contracts deleted. Archived counts the credit-bearing contracts among them, whose usage proof the capture trigger copied to st_provider_usage_archive in the same statement. Zero while the mode is off or dry run. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: contracts kept / s by reason
panels.description: Contracts past the horizon that the pass read and kept, each under the first reason that holds it: open (no outcome), unresolved (disputed), recent_close (closed inside the horizon), busy (another transaction holds the contract or a sweep), unsettled (an escrow is not settled), payment_hold, payment_incomplete and payment_recent (a sweep's payment holds retention, is not settled (completed, or closed by the USDC close-out), or completed within CompletedContractExpiration), unpaid_legacy (an unpaid sweep on a contract minted before the earning cutoff), plan_staged (a sweep staged in a pending payment plan), block_points (an unpaid sweep in an operator block whose points can still be awarded) and payment_review (a sweep whose payment completed under attribution review, which stamps no retention on its contracts). Counted in dry run and on. The pass rereads what it kept when it starts over: a pass that reached the horizon restarts 30 days after it began.

panels.title: pass lag, cursor and horizon
panels.description: Left axis: how far the pass's cursor is behind the horizon. Right axis: the cursor, the mint time of the last contract the pass committed past, and the horizon, before which a contract minted and closed is past it. The cursor climbs to the horizon while the pass catches up, then both move with the clock. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_lag_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: contracts scanned and eligible / s by mode
panels.description: Contracts the pass read, and those that passed every check, by mode. In on mode each eligible contract was deleted; a dry run reads ahead of the stored cursor and deletes nothing. Scanned less eligible is the contracts kept beside. The pass reads at most maxRowsPerSecond from the control (200 a second by default, 2000 at most).

panels.title: batch transaction duration p50 / p99 and batch size
panels.description: Left axis: the median and 99th percentile of one batch transaction, by mode, ok and failed batches together. A batch slower than 10 seconds halves the next one, one under 2.5 seconds grows it by half, and each statement stops at 30 seconds. Right axis: the adaptive contracts per batch that the newest run's taskworker last used, between 125 and the control's batchSize (2000 at most). Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_batch_size{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: reaper runs, failed batches and rollup clamps in the trailing hour
panels.description: Runs that ended in the trailing hour, by why: budget (the run spent its 10-minute budget with work left), horizon (the pass reached the horizon), off (the mode is off), control_unavailable (the Redis control could not be read; the run stops as if off), canceled (the task context ended; the batch in flight rolled back) and error (a batch failed; the retry resumes at the last committed batch). Failed batches count the batch transactions that ended in an error, by mode. Rollup clamps count the transfer audit rollup runs that resumed at the first day the reaper cannot reach (model.TransferAuditRollupFirstDay, about 33 days back: the reaper's 35-day floor less a 2-day margin) instead of the day their chain stood at, leaving the rows of the days before as they were. Any means the chain fell weeks behind.

panels.title: due contracts deleted / s
panels.description: Contracts the delete pass of RemoveCompletedContracts deleted, each with its close reports, closes, escrows, sweeps and extender parties: contracts whose reap_time has passed (seven days after their payment completed, or stragglers past 300 days) that no payment holds. Counted at commit. A batch reads at most 2,000 due contracts and the pass is paced to 200 a second inside its five-minute budget, once per run (about every 30 to 50 minutes), so the rate comes in bursts. Each credit-bearing contract deleted is archived to st_provider_usage_archive. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: due-contract delete pass stops by reason in the trailing hour
panels.description: Delete passes that ended in the trailing hour, by why: drained (no contract was due), budget (the pass spent its five-minute budget, or the run its 20-minute budget, with work left), busy (another writer owned a balance of the batch's escrows), lock_timeout (a lock wait reached 2 s; the batch rolled back) and statement_timeout (a statement was canceled, at 30 s or by an operator; the batch rolled back). One pass per RemoveCompletedContracts run. A lock or statement stop leaves the work to the next run; repeated ones mean contention or a slow plan.

panels.title: close evidence rows deleted / s
panels.description: Close evidence rows the contract task's row retention (RemoveExpiredCloseEvidence) deleted: reports accepted longer ago than the retention, whose contract is resolved or gone, whether or not the contract horizon reaper keeps the contract. Counted per committed batch, each reading at most 5,000 rows in the census index's order and deleting the expired ones by ctid. The deletes take a third of each contract task run and are paced by their own brake, the Redis hash {close_evidence_retention}control (mode on or off, maxRowsPerSecond), read before every batch: 1,000 rows a second without it, 5,000 at most, and none with the mode off, a rate of 0 or the hash unreadable. bringyourctl db close-evidence-retention shows and sets it. Below about 83 rows a second a batch reads fewer rows, so the rate holds. Whole weeks the partition drop takes are not counted, and that drop never reads the brake. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: close evidence retention by taskworker (days)
panels.description: The retention each taskworker's last close evidence row retention run applied, in days: the contract horizon reaper's horizonDays while the reaper's mode is on, never less than the installed evidence guard admits (35 days once the horizon guard migration is applied, 91 before), and 91 days with the mode off or in a dry run, or when the reaper's control cannot be read. A taskworker keeps its last run's value until its next run, so an instance that has not run the contract task lately shows an older value. With the mode on, 35 days permanently deletes the evidence of every resolved or deleted contract accepted more than 35 days ago. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: close evidence row retention stops by reason in the trailing hour
panels.description: Close evidence row retention runs that ended in the trailing hour, by why, one per contract task run: done (a pass finished and the retention is caught up; the next run follows in 15 minutes), budget (the run's deadline or pace ended it with work left; the next run follows in a minute), brake_off (the brake's mode is off or its rate is 0; nothing goes until it lifts, and the task looks again in 15 minutes), brake_unread (the brake could not be read, so nothing more went that run; logged at V(1)), lock_timeout (a batch's lock wait reached 2 s and it rolled back), statement_timeout (a batch's statement was canceled, at 30 s or by an operator, and it rolled back), canceled (the run's context ended) and error (anything else failed; the log says what). A brake left off shows as brake_off, where a caught-up retention shows as done. A lock or statement stop leaves the work to the next run; repeated ones mean contention or a slow plan. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: expired rows deleted / s by table
panels.description: Rows the expiry and retention tasks deleted, by table: rate-limit attempts, auth resets, device add history, network name reclaims, provider blackhole checks and bandwidth quota buckets, and the extender release ledger. Each committed batch of at most 10,000 rows counts under its table; one cleanup runs for at most 30 seconds and leaves the rest of a backlog to its next run. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: provider totals drain rows and passes / s
panels.description: Queued provider-total allocations the drain_legacy_provider_totals chain read, by outcome after an acknowledged commit: credited (added to the provider account and removed), applied (the per-task reader had already credited it; removed without a credit) or left (claimed, held, changed or invalid; the per-task reader keeps it). Drained rows are deleted, not moved to finished_task, so task finishes per second fall below submissions without any task lost. Passes by result: ok (acknowledged, including passes that found nothing) or error (failed or unacknowledged; nothing is assumed applied). provider_totals.yml (drain.enabled, drain.rows_per_second, 4,000 by default) pauses or paces the drain without a deploy. A persistent left count with an old queue head means rows the per-task reader still holds or cannot apply.

panels.title: provider totals drain lag behind now
panels.description: Now less the creation time of the last queued provider total the drain visited, from its task id: the drain's lag. It stays at least a minute behind by design, since the walk leaves ids younger than a minute for a later pass. Only the taskworker running the chain updates the position, so this reads the latest across taskworkers. It grows while the drain is paused or failing; the per-task reader then applies the rows, each 5 minutes after it was queued. No data before a taskworker ran the chain. Settlement stops queueing provider totals with the 2026-11-11 billing split change (BILLING-SPLIT.md), so once the rows queued before it are drained the position stops moving and this lag grows by design.

panels.title: retention mode
panels.description: The mode the newest prober retention run last read from its Redis control {prober_retention}control, which a run rereads before every pass: off counts the backlog and drops nothing; dry run reads one page of due passes and counts the contracts a drop would delete, changing nothing; on drops each due pass, oldest first: its zero-byte contracts, then its identity, then its registry row. The code default is off, so a deploy drops nothing until an operator sets the mode; a mode that does not parse, or maxContractsPerSecond or maxShardsPerMinute at zero, is off too. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_prober_retention_mode{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: generations kept
panels.description: Generations of probe passes the retention keeps, the current one included: UTC days, as the newest run's control read set them (retainedGenerations, 2 to 30; the code's 8 while the control sets none; a value that does not parse keeps 30). Passes created before the cutoff, the start of the oldest day kept, are in dropped generations. The control cannot keep fewer than two, so a pass in flight never falls out of the window. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_prober_retention_retained_generations{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: cutoff (first pass create time kept)
panels.description: The first pass create time the retention keeps: the start of the oldest UTC day kept, 7 days before the newest run's own with 8 generations kept. Every pass created before it is in a dropped generation, and is dropped once its deadline is 6 hours past. It moves a day forward at each UTC midnight. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_prober_retention_cutoff_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: passes due in dropped generations
panels.description: Registered probe passes created before the cutoff and not closed, counted at the start of the newest run: the drop's backlog, including passes waiting out a refusal (retried after an hour) or a failed step (retried after a minute). While the drop keeps up it rises at each UTC midnight by the day that fell out of the window and falls back within hours; off and dry run drop nothing. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_prober_retention_due_shards{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: oldest pass behind the cutoff
panels.description: The cutoff less the create time of the oldest registered pass not closed, both from the newest run's start: how far the drop is behind. Zero once no pass before the cutoff remains. While the drop keeps up it rises to about a day at each UTC midnight and falls back as the drop takes the newly dropped generation, oldest first. Past a day the drop is behind, off, or holding passes it refuses (see refusals by reason). Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(clamp_min(urnetwork_prober_retention_cutoff_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} - urnetwork_prober_retention_oldest_shard_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}, 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: newest run started
panels.description: When the newest prober retention run any taskworker still reports started: the run clock it published once it read its control and its backlog. A run lasts about 4 minutes at most; the next follows 15 seconds later while passes remain due, and 5 minutes later once none is due, the mode is off or dry run, or the control could not be read. A start older than about 10 minutes means the chain is not running, and the other retention stats show No data past 30 minutes. A run that cannot read its control or its backlog publishes no clock.

panels.title: passes / s by outcome and refusals by reason
panels.description: Probe passes of dropped generations the retention took up, by outcome: dropped (its zero-byte contracts, identity and registry row are gone), blocked (its identity transaction refused it; retried after an hour), error (a step failed; retried a minute later while the run goes on to the next pass), deferred (the run's budget ended inside its contract step; a later run reads its contracts again), gone (another run dropped it first) and dry_run (a dry run read it). Refusals by the first reason found: active (the pass is still live), unresolved (a contract it funded has no outcome), unsettled (an escrow of its network is not settled, or a debit is still journaled), balance (its network holds a balance that is not a plain grant, or one that arrived during the check), hosted (a client of its network owns a hosted proxy resource) and connected (a client of its network is connected). On mode drops at most maxShardsPerMinute passes a minute (30 by default, 600 at most). Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: contracts deleted and kept / s by outcome
panels.description: Resolved contracts of dropped passes that the contract step read, closed before the cutoff, by outcome: deleted (with its close reports, closes, escrows, sweeps and extender parties, in one short transaction), kept_bytes (its destination close carries bytes or it has a sweep: left to the contract horizon reaper, since byte sums read it), kept_unsettled (an escrow is not settled), busy (another transaction holds it, or it changed since it was read) and eligible_dry_run (a dry run would delete it). Archived counts the settled or dispute-resolved contracts among those deleted, whose usage proof the capture trigger copied to st_provider_usage_archive in the same statement. The step reads at most maxContractsPerSecond (200 a second by default, 2000 at most) in batches of 500; contracts off in the control skips it. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: rows deleted / s by table
panels.description: Rows the retention deleted, by table. The contract step deletes contract_close_report, contract_close, transfer_escrow, transfer_escrow_sweep, contract_extender and transfer_contract rows; the identity step deletes the pass's clients with their client_tls_certificate, network_client_role, network_client_provider_intent, network_client_connection, network_client_location_reliability and provide_key rows, then its device, transfer_balance, network, network_user_auth_seedphrase and network_user rows; the registry step deletes the prober_shard_run rows of dropped generations whose pass closed. Zero while the mode is off or dry run. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: backlog: passes due and lag behind the cutoff
panels.description: Left axis: registered passes created before the cutoff and not closed, at the start of the newest run. Right axis: the cutoff less the create time of the oldest pass not closed, zero once none before the cutoff remains. While the drop keeps up both rise at each UTC midnight, as a generation falls out of the window, and fall back within hours; passes due beside a lag that does not fall are passes the identity transaction keeps refusing (see refusals by reason). Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read its control and its backlog.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_prober_retention_due_shards{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

max(clamp_min(urnetwork_prober_retention_cutoff_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} - urnetwork_prober_retention_oldest_shard_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}, 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_prober_retention_run_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: step duration p50 / p99 by step
panels.description: The median and 99th percentile of one retention step, by step, ok and failed together: select (a page of due passes, locked in on mode), contracts (one contract batch: the window read, the locked classification and the deletes; its statements stop at 30 seconds and wait at most 2 seconds for a lock), identity (the pass's identity transaction) and registry (one registry row, or a batch of up to 1000 closed rows of dropped generations). Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: runs and failed steps in the trailing hour
panels.description: Runs that ended in the trailing hour, by why: caught_up (no pass of a dropped generation is due), budget (the run spent its 4-minute budget with passes left), off (the mode is off), dry_run (a dry run read its one page), control_unavailable (the Redis control could not be read; the run stops at once), canceled (the task context ended) and error (the backlog read, a page read or the registry cleanup failed; the task retries). Failed steps count the steps that ended in an error, by step; a pass whose step failed is retried a minute later while the run goes on to the next.

panels.title: orphan sweep passes that kept contract_participant unexamined (7 days)
panels.description: Passes of the orphan contract sweep (SweepOrphanContractData, a weekly taskworker pass spread over resume runs) in the trailing 7 days whose contract_participant step kept every row unexamined: contract_participant has rows, and no valid btree index on transfer_contract leading with stream_id (transfer_contract_stream_id, v629, dropped while contract_participant is empty) answers the step's parent probe, so the step does not run rather than read the whole contract heap once per row. Zero while multi-hop contracts are off and contract_participant is empty. Anything above zero means participant rows exist without that index: restore it, or give the step a parent probe that does not read transfer_contract by stream_id. Each refusal is also logged once per pass. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: unique-exit proxies: assignments, allocations, replacements, supply and lifetime (sweep_proxy_exits)
fresh unique-exit assignments by state
panels.description: Assignments not released, as the sweep_proxy_exits task last counted them (every 30 s, on any one replica; samples older than 120 s are dropped). pending until the device confirms its exit through its own tunnel, active once confirmed, replacing while a failed exit waits for a replacement (a cap, no supply, or manual mode).

targets.expr: max by (state) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_assignments{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_sweep_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_sweep_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: unique-exit allocations / s by service and result
panels.description: assigned: a proxy pinned to a new unique exit (api and alt on create and rotate, taskworker on replacement). no_supply: no exit the network could take in the location. collision_retry: a candidate another allocation held or took first, skipped for the next.

panels.title: unique-exit replacements per hour by reason
panels.description: Proxies moved to a new unique exit: offline (provider lost past the 120 s grace), unreachable (the device's confirms failed), verdict (blackhole or TLS authentication, no grace), collision (the exit now matches another of the network's exits, no grace), rotate (the customer's request, through api or alt). Failures are capped at 6 an hour per proxy and 10% an hour per network.

panels.title: fresh unique-exit supply: distinct egress keys, top 15 countries
panels.description: Distinct provider egress keys (an exact IPv4 address or IPv6 /64, keyed; the address is never stored) observed in the last 24 h, by country: the most unique exits one network could hold there. Farms behind one address count once. Set every 10 minutes by the sweep; samples older than 25 minutes are dropped.

targets.expr: topk(15, max by (country) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_keys{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1500 and urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30)))

panels.title: unique-exit assignment lifetime
panels.description: How long an assignment lived when it was released: replaced, rotated, or its proxy removed.

panels.title: sweep_proxy_exits snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since any taskworker replica last finished a unique-exit sweep (every 30 s) and last set the supply gauges (every 10 minutes).

panels.title: SN25 extender pool: Z, Z', N, M by phase (controller/st_ledger_v2_extender_metrics.go)
extender pool bytes by phase and part
panels.description: The extender pool's bytes in the last epoch of each phase: build (an epoch the amendment covers, as its root first builds it) and shadow (an epoch before E_x, as its shadow report builds it). pool is Z, intra_platform and intra_network its parts, weight Z' after the cap, eligible_provider W_k, and unfunded and measurement the pooled shares Z leaves out.

panels.title: extender pool counts by phase
panels.description: N (eligible) and M (units), the census rows, the contracts and payer networks behind Z, the contracts left out, and the platform endpoints registered, in the last epoch of each phase (census, build, shadow).

panels.title: extenders' share of the pool weight
panels.description: Z' / (W_k + Z') in the last epoch of each phase: at most 0.5 under the cap (zeta 1), 0 when no extender is eligible.

panels.title: extender pool epoch by phase
panels.description: The epoch the extender pool gauges describe: census (captured at the epoch's end), build and shadow.
